topics.title: 16.1.1 Improving Spatial Locality
topics.summary: Spatial locality means using nearby data while the fetched region is useful. Contiguous containers often help sequential traversal because adjacent elements occupy adjacent storage. A pointer-rich structure can scatter logically related values across allocations, making a traversal require more independent memory fetches.

An array of complete records can be excellent when every operation needs all fields, while a columnar layout can be better when an operation touches only one field across many records. topics.title: 16.1.2 Improving Temporal Locality
topics.summary: Temporal locality means reusing data before it is displaced from fast storage. Blocking or tiling can keep a working subset active while performing several operations on it. Recomputing or reloading a large intermediate between distant stages can lose that opportunity.

topics.title: Improving Spatial Locality by Traversing Contiguous Rows
topics.summary: Row-major traversal consumes adjacent elements while they are already in nearby cache lines, demonstrating spatial locality with a simple contiguous representation.

blocks.text: Improving Spatial Locality by Traversing Contiguous Rows
rich: Improving Spatial Locality by Traversing Contiguous Rows
blocks.headingContext: Improving Spatial Locality by Traversing Contiguous Rows

blocks.text: Purpose
Row-major traversal consumes adjacent elements while they are already in nearby cache lines, demonstrating spatial locality with a simple contiguous representation.
rich: Row-major traversal consumes adjacent elements while they are already in nearby cache lines, demonstrating spatial locality with a simple contiguous representation.

blocks.text: Code or command
What the important parts do

`r*cols+c` maps a two-dimensional logical coordinate into one contiguous row-major vector. Incrementing `c` touches the next integer in memory, allowing each fetched cache line to contribute several useful values.
rich: `r*cols+c` maps a two-dimensional logical coordinate into one contiguous row-major vector. Incrementing `c` touches the next integer in memory, allowing each fetched cache line to contribute several useful values.

blocks.text: Expected behavior or output
The program prints `1048576`.
Concrete experiment
Swap the loop order so columns are outermost. Benchmark both orders for larger matrices and compare cache-miss counts.
rich: Swap the loop order so columns are outermost. Benchmark both orders for larger matrices and compare cache-miss counts.

topics.title: 16.2.1 Comparing Arrays of Structures
topics.summary: An array of structures keeps each entity’s fields together. It is natural for object-level access, serialization adapters, and code that repeatedly needs complete records. Its stride includes all fields and padding, even when a particular loop uses only one measurement field.

topics.title: 16.2.2 Comparing Structures of Arrays
topics.summary: A structure of arrays stores each field in its own contiguous sequence. A loop over one field can then traverse a dense stream of relevant values, and vectorization may become easier. The tradeoff is maintaining correspondence between columns and handling operations that need several fields together.

topics.title: Comparing Array-of-Structures with Structure-of-Arrays Layout
topics.summary: When a workload processes only one field, structure-of-arrays can pack that field contiguously instead of dragging unrelated members through the memory hierarchy.

blocks.text: Comparing Array-of-Structures with Structure-of-Arrays Layout
Purpose
When a workload processes only one field, structure-of-arrays can pack that field contiguously instead of dragging unrelated members through the memory hierarchy.
rich: When a workload processes only one field, structure-of-arrays can pack that field contiguously instead of dragging unrelated members through the memory hierarchy.

blocks.text: Code or command
What the important parts do
The AoS vector interleaves x, y, z, and mass for each particle. The SoA representation gives x its own dense array. Both represent equivalent logical data but create different memory-access patterns.
rich: The AoS vector interleaves x, y, z, and mass for each particle. The SoA representation gives x its own dense array. Both represent equivalent logical data but create different memory-access patterns.

blocks.text: Expected behavior or output
Both sums print `1000`.
Concrete experiment
Expand each particle with additional cold fields and benchmark an x-only transform. Then benchmark a workload that needs all fields to see when AoS can become competitive again.
